UnitStatement: The equation-bbox-detect brief is an INIT-TASK shape rendered by tools/equation_audit/build_equation_bbox_brief.py.
The equation-bbox-detect worker receives the rendered brief verbatim through TASK.
The bbox worker detects display-equation bounding boxes on one page and emits normalized coordinates for downstream cropping.
ScopePath identifies the absolute path to the page-work directory.
The equation-bbox-detect brief authorizes OUTPUT_PATH as the only write target.
IMAGE_PATH is the absolute path to the raster page_NNNN.png input.
PAGE_MD_PATH is the absolute path to the per-page Markdown input.
PAGE_NUM is the page number integer supplied to the bbox worker.
OUTPUT_PATH is the absolute path where page_NNNN_eq_bboxes.json is written.
EXPECTED_EQUATION_HASHES may be empty or contain expected 12-hex equation hashes.
Workers identify display equations visible on the page raster as block-level math typically set off from running prose.
Workers must not box inline equations or symbols inside running text.
Workers emit normalized bbox coordinates in [0,1] relative to the page raster width and height.
Boxes should tightly enclose the display equation without including surrounding paragraph text.
Each emitted equation index is 1-based and ordered top-to-bottom on the page.
latex_excerpt records the first approximately 20 characters of visible LaTeX or symbolic content for cross-checking.
If a page has no display equations, the worker writes an empty equations list and returns RUN_STATUS=NO_FINDINGS.
IMAGE_PATH must be an absolute path to an existing .png file.
PAGE_MD_PATH must be an absolute path to an existing .md file.
PAGE_NUM must be at least 1 and match the NNNN page number embedded in IMAGE_PATH.
OUTPUT_PATH must be absolute, end in .json, and have an existing parent directory.
Each EXPECTED_EQUATION_HASHES entry must be a 12-character lowercase hexadecimal string.
The output JSON object must match the schema consumed by tools/equation_audit/crop_equation_regions.py.
On failed input validation, the worker writes an empty equations list with a short error reason.
The bbox coordinate origin (0,0) is the top-left of the page raster.
The bbox coordinate point (1,1) is the bottom-right of the page raster.
bbox_norm is [x0,y0,x1,y1] with x0 less than x1 and y0 less than y1.
Every bbox_norm coordinate is a float in the closed interval [0.0,1.0].
The downstream crop tool adds a default 0.005 padding ring, so worker boxes should be visually tight rather than padded.
The bbox worker returns one of SUCCESS, NO_FINDINGS, FAILED_INPUTS, or FAILED.
The bbox worker reports PAGE_NUM and EQUATION_COUNT with its run status.
When expected equation hashes are supplied, worker findings must be ordered to support positional cross-checking.
The persona pairs equations[i].latex_excerpt with the i-th equation in equations.jsonl for the page.
The persona does not require exact excerpt matches, but flags large mismatches for human review.
The worker does not compute equation hashes; EXPECTED_EQUATION_HASHES supports persona cross-checking after dispatch.
Exactly one file should exist at OUTPUT_PATH after an equation-bbox-detect run.
The equation-bbox-detect worker must not create or modify files outside the declared write boundary.
The bbox output file must be a single JSON object, not a list or JSON-lines stream.
The top-level page field is required, must equal PAGE_NUM, and must be at least 1.
The top-level equations field is a possibly empty list with one entry per detected display equation.
The top-level error field is present only on FAILED_INPUTS runs.
Each equations entry has a 1-based integer index that is strictly increasing within the list.
Each bbox_norm entry is exactly four floats in [0.0,1.0] with x0 less than x1 and y0 less than y1.
latex_excerpt is an optional freeform hint and is not authoritative equation transcription.
bbox_norm coordinate values must be floats, not integers or strings.
A valid equation box should have width and height each at least approximately 1 percent of the page.
A valid equation box should not exceed approximately 95 percent of the page width.
A typical single-line display-equation box should not exceed approximately 25 percent of the page height.
A multi-line display-equation box may exceed typical single-line height but should remain below approximately 50 percent of page height.
Consecutive equation boxes must be ordered top-to-bottom by nondecreasing y0 coordinate.
Two distinct equation boxes with pairwise IoU greater than 0.1 are a detection error and should be merged.
A worker may include or exclude far-right equation numbers, but the choice must be consistent across the page.
When EXPECTED_EQUATION_HASHES is non-empty, the number of emitted equations should equal the number of expected hashes.
A mismatch between emitted equation count and expected hash count is non-fatal and is surfaced for human review.
A wildly different latex_excerpt suggests either top-to-bottom ordering disagreement or equations visible on the page but absent from Markdown extraction.
The worker emits bbox findings and the persona reconciles cross-check mismatches.
RUN_STATUS=SUCCESS means at least one display equation was detected and all invariants pass.
RUN_STATUS=NO_FINDINGS means the page contains no display equations and the equations list is empty.
RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS means required inputs were missing or malformed and the output includes an error field.
RUN_STATUS=FAILED means an unexpected failure occurred, such as an unreadable image or write-boundary violation.
A missing or unparseable bbox output file blocks downstream crop generation.
A top-level page value different from PAGE_NUM can cause the crop tool to write to the wrong page filename.
Any bbox_norm outside [0,1] or violating x0<x1 or y0<y1 blocks downstream crop generation.
Non-monotonic or gapped equation indexes block downstream crop generation.
Severe overlap between two equation boxes, defined as IoU greater than 0.5, blocks downstream crop generation.
Writing output anywhere other than OUTPUT_PATH blocks downstream crop generation.
Worker stdout and RUN_STATUS are sufficient evidence for routine success.
FAILED and FAILED_INPUTS runs require the status explanation as evidence.
For NO_FINDINGS runs, the empty equations list is the evidence.
Visual-quality checks use produced PNG crops as evidence during Gate 2 review.
The equation-bbox-detect skill reads one rasterized page PNG, identifies every display equation, and emits normalized bounding-box coordinates.
The equation-bbox-detect skill writes page_NNNN_eq_bboxes.json for consumption by crop_equation_regions.py.
The skill closes the missing upstream producer for the per-page bbox JSONs expected by crop_equation_regions.py.
The skill runs under TASK in generic shell mode when EQUATION_AUDIT enables per-equation crops during Phase 1.
The skill is not the correct worker for interpreting per-equation human notes, figure/table bboxes, inline-equation detection, or cross-page reasoning.
Required inputs are IMAGE_PATH, PAGE_MD_PATH, PAGE_NUM, and OUTPUT_PATH.
EXPECTED_EQUATION_HASHES are extracted by audit_equations.py and are used for cross-check notes in latex_excerpt.
The skill read boundary is limited to IMAGE_PATH and PAGE_MD_PATH.
The skill must not read other pages, equations.jsonl, other source files, skeletons, assets, or sidecars.
The skill write boundary is exactly one file: OUTPUT_PATH.
The equation-bbox-detect skill has no side effects beyond writing OUTPUT_PATH.
No deterministic tools are invoked by the equation-bbox-detect worker.
The worker uses native Read for the page PNG and page Markdown and native Write for the output JSON.
The worker must not shell out to a subprocess or external command.
The worker must not widen scope beyond the assigned page.
The worker must not modify page Markdown or audit artifacts.
The worker must not re-OCR body text outside display equations.
Input validation confirms the PNG input, Markdown input, and output parent directory before bbox detection proceeds.
The worker scans PAGE_MD_PATH for display-math blocks to know which equations are expected on the page.
The page Markdown equation list is context for cross-checking, not ground truth for bbox extraction.
The worker loads the single assigned page raster before identifying display-equation regions.
Display equations are block-level math set off from surrounding prose, often centered, spaced apart, or numbered at the right margin.
Inline math embedded in running sentences must not be boxed as a display equation.
Section headings, table cells, figure labels, and page numbers must not be boxed as display equations.
For each display equation, the worker determines the tightest axis-aligned rectangle enclosing its typeset content.
Normalized coordinates use x0,y0 for the top-left corner and x1,y1 for the bottom-right corner.
The worker captures only a short latex_excerpt hint and must not attempt full LaTeX transcription.
The skill targets display equations only and must not detect inline math inside running prose.
The skill emits normalized coordinates only; pixel coordinates are forbidden.
Each equation-bbox-detect invocation is page-local and carries no cross-page state.
EQUATION_AUDIT runs audit_equations.py to extract display equations per page into equations.jsonl before bbox dispatch.
EQUATION_AUDIT renders one bbox brief per page that has display equations, optionally embedding EXPECTED_EQUATION_HASHES.
EQUATION_AUDIT dispatches one TASK plus equation-bbox-detect invocation per page.
EQUATION_AUDIT collects page_NNNN_eq_bboxes.json files from page work directories.
EQUATION_AUDIT runs crop_equation_regions.py to emit per-equation PNG crops from bbox outputs.
EQUATION_AUDIT embeds equation crops in audit HTML for visual review.
equation-bbox-detect follows the same per-page VLM fanout pattern as pdf2md-page-assets and drawing-extract-page, narrowed to display equations.
The tool policy frames equation-bbox-detect as VLM vision reasoning over the page raster with optional page-Markdown cross-checking.
TASK does not whitelist deterministic tools for equation-bbox-detect.
The worker uses Read to load both IMAGE_PATH and PAGE_MD_PATH.
The worker uses Write to write the single OUTPUT_PATH JSON file.
The surrounding PDF2MD pipeline uses rasterize_pdf.py to produce page_NNNN.png inputs.
The surrounding EQUATION_AUDIT pipeline uses audit_equations.py to extract display equations and populate EXPECTED_EQUATION_HASHES.
The surrounding EQUATION_AUDIT pipeline uses build_equation_bbox_brief.py to produce bbox briefs.
The surrounding EQUATION_AUDIT pipeline uses crop_equation_regions.py to consume bbox JSONs and emit crops.
The bbox worker writes its JSON output and the persona feeds that output to crop_equation_regions.py.
Worker reasoning begins by reading the assigned page raster.
Worker reasoning uses the page Markdown display-math blocks as expected-equation context.
Worker reasoning determines the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that encloses equation content while excluding surrounding text and separate equation numbers.
latex_excerpt is a hint for persona cross-checking against EXPECTED_EQUATION_HASHES, not authoritative transcription.
The worker must not invoke Bash, python3, shell-outs, subprocesses, or other deterministic commands.
The worker must not write outside OUTPUT_PATH.
The worker must not read outside IMAGE_PATH and PAGE_MD_PATH.
The worker must not box section headings, table cells, figure labels, page numbers, or running headers.
The worker must not emit pixel coordinates.
The OUTPUT_PATH parent directory must already exist because the skill does not create directories.
A write-boundary violation causes RUN_STATUS=FAILED rather than a workaround.
